public_rationale: Reduced ramp-up fees are documented, but their existence does not establish that they caused all of the projected profit. The savings are unquantified, and no matching reconciliation excludes improvements in the business. The exclusive causal claim remains unproven.
limitations: The accessible contract evidence is reputable reporting rather than a readable primary filing.
Neither lower fees nor a later reported profit alone establishes the cause of the May projection.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Anthropic's reported Q2 2026 operating profit comes from accounting (a discounted SpaceX compute rate), not from any improvement in its business model.

statement.excerpt: That operating profit is a result of accountancy rather than any improvements to its business model.

from_speaker: rather than any improvements to its business model
our_interpretation: Assess the cause of the Q2 operating profit projected in May, not whether Anthropic ultimately reported any profit under another definition.
Read the claimed mechanism as temporary SpaceX ramp-up savings sufficient to eliminate the projected profit if removed, without improved underlying operating economics.
A lower contractual bill alone does not establish an accounting manipulation or exclude other improvements.
Use the post's explicit non-GAAP characterization without assuming that EBITDA and operating income are interchangeable.
criteria.support_condition: A reconciliation on the forecast's accounting basis shows that temporary ramp-up savings account for the projected operating profit and that underlying operating economics did not improve.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A comparable reconciliation shows positive operating profit after removing the temporary benefit, or establishes that underlying operating improvements materially contributed contrary to the exclusive attribution.
